title: Why Drug Companies are Looking to Space for New Medicines
subtitle: Manufacturing in orbit could change how we treat serious illnesses like cancer.

summary.en: Pharmaceutical companies are beginning to use space to create new types of medicine. By using the weightless environment of orbit, scientists can grow better crystals for drugs. This process is different from making medicine on Earth because gravity does not interfere with the growth. While the International Space Station has helped with early research, companies are now building their own space factories. Experts believe this could lead to more effective treatments for patients in the future.
summary.zh: 製藥公司正開始利用太空來開發新型藥物。透過利用軌道上的無重力環境，科學家可以培育出品質更好的藥物晶體。此過程與在地球上製造藥物不同，因為重力不會干擾晶體的生長。雖然國際太空站已協助早期的研究，但目前各公司正著手建造屬於自己的太空工廠。專家認為，這將有助於未來為患者提供更有效的治療方式。

paragraphs.en: High above the Earth, about 300 miles away, three small capsules are currently orbiting our planet. These machines, each about the size of a washing machine, are not just floating in space for fun. Inside one of them, scientists are growing tiny crystals that could one day become a powerful new cancer drug. This project is a major step toward a new and potentially profitable industry: making medicine in space.
paragraphs.zh: 在地球上方約三百英里處，有三個小型太空艙正環繞著我們的星球運行。這些機器的大小與洗衣機相當，它們並非只是為了好玩而漂浮在太空中。在其中一個太空艙內，科學家正在培育微小的晶體，這些晶體有朝一日可能成為強效的新型癌症藥物。這項計畫是邁向一個新興且具備獲利潛力產業的重要一步：在太空中製造藥物。

paragraphs.en: The company behind this project is Varda Space Industries, based in California. According to The Guardian Health, the company launched two of these capsules on October 1st and a third one on October 20th. This is the first time a company has had three spacecraft in orbit at the same time for this purpose. Will Bruey, the chief executive of Varda, said that while this idea once seemed like a dream for the future, it is now becoming a reality as the number of launches increases.
paragraphs.zh: 這項計畫背後的公司是總部位於加州的瓦達太空工業公司（Varda Space Industries）。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，該公司於十月一日發射了其中兩個太空艙，並於十月二十日發射了第三個。這是一家公司首次為了此類目的，同時讓三艘太空船在軌道上運行。瓦達公司的執行長威爾·布魯伊（Will Bruey）表示，雖然這個想法曾經看似遙不可及的夢想，但隨著發射次數的增加，它正逐漸成為現實。

paragraphs.en: Why would a company want to make medicine in space instead of on Earth? The answer lies in a condition called microgravity—a state where there is very little gravity. On Earth, gravity causes particles in liquids to settle at the bottom, and it creates currents that move liquids around. These natural forces can make it difficult to grow perfect crystals. When scientists grow crystals in space, they can avoid these problems. Dr. Meganne Christian, a mission manager at the UK-based Satellite Applications Catapult, explained that without the interference of gravity, crystals can grow in a much more organized and perfect way.
paragraphs.zh: 為什麼公司會想在太空中而不是在地球上製造藥物？答案在於一種稱為「微重力」的狀態，即重力極小的環境。在地球上，重力會導致液體中的顆粒沉澱到底部，並產生擾動液體的對流。這些自然力量會使培育完美的晶體變得困難。當科學家在太空中培育晶體時，就能避免這些問題。英國衛星應用彈射器公司（Satellite Applications Catapult）的任務經理梅根·克里斯汀博士（Dr. Meganne Christian）解釋說，在沒有重力干擾的情況下，晶體能以更有序、更完美的方式生長。

paragraphs.en: This is very important for pharmaceutical companies. The way a drug crystal is shaped and arranged can change how well the medicine works. It affects how easily a drug dissolves in the body, how long it stays stable, and how it is given to a patient. If scientists can make better crystals in space, they might be able to change some medicines that currently require long hospital stays for intravenous infusions—where medicine is given through a tube into a vein—into simple injections that patients can give themselves at home.
paragraphs.zh: 這對製藥公司來說至關重要。藥物晶體的形狀與排列方式會影響藥效。它會影響藥物在體內的溶解難易度、穩定性，以及給藥方式。如果科學家能在太空中製造出更好的晶體，或許就能將某些目前需要長時間住院進行靜脈輸注（即透過管子將藥物注入靜脈）的藥物，轉變為患者可以在家中自行施打的簡單注射劑。

paragraphs.en: Medicine is not the only thing that could be made in space. Other materials, such as semiconductors used in smartphones and electric cars, could also benefit from this process. Dr. Christian noted that materials like graphene, which is very strong and useful, often have defects when made on Earth. By making these materials in microgravity, companies could produce much higher-performing products with fewer errors.
paragraphs.zh: 藥物並非唯一能在太空中製造的東西。其他材料，例如用於智慧型手機和電動車的半導體，也能從這個過程中受益。克里斯汀博士指出，像石墨烯這種非常堅固且實用的材料，在地球上製造時往往會出現缺陷。透過在微重力環境下製造這些材料，公司可以生產出效能更高且瑕疵更少的產品。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have been studying these processes for decades, mostly on the International Space Station (ISS). However, the ISS was not built for large-scale manufacturing. Dr. Ryan Reeves, a scientist for the ISS National Laboratory, explained that the station was designed as a place for scientific experiments, not as a factory. Furthermore, the ISS is expected to be retired around 2030. Because of this, several companies are now working to build their own commercial space stations and specialized laboratories to take over the work.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家研究這些製程已有數十年之久，主要是在國際太空站（ISS）上進行。然而，國際太空站並非為大規模製造而建造。國際太空站國家實驗室（ISS National Laboratory）的科學家萊恩·里夫斯博士（Dr. Ryan Reeves）解釋說，該站的設計初衷是作為科學實驗場所，而非工廠。此外，國際太空站預計將於二〇三〇年左右退役。因此，目前有幾家公司正致力於建造自己的商業太空站與專業實驗室，以接手相關工作。

paragraphs.en: One example is the UK-based company BioOrbit. They recently sent a small laboratory to the ISS to test the production of cancer drugs that patients could inject themselves. However, experts point out that there are still challenges to overcome. For large-scale production, companies need to find ways to run these factories without humans present. Humans can introduce dirt or other contaminants into the sensitive environment, which could ruin the delicate crystal-growing process. Therefore, the goal is to create automated systems that can work alone in space.
paragraphs.zh: 英國公司生物軌道（BioOrbit）就是一個例子。他們最近將一個小型實驗室送往國際太空站，以測試患者可自行注射的癌症藥物生產。然而，專家指出仍有挑戰需要克服。對於大規模生產，公司需要找到在無人值守的情況下運作這些工廠的方法。人類可能會將灰塵或其他污染物帶入敏感環境中，這可能會破壞脆弱的晶體生長過程。因此，目標是建立能在太空中獨立運作的自動化系統。

paragraphs.en: As these companies continue to test their technology, the dream of "space manufacturing" is moving closer to reality. While it is still a new field, the potential benefits for patients are significant. If researchers can successfully create more stable and effective drugs in the weightless environment of orbit, it could change the way we treat many serious diseases. For now, the world is watching these small capsules as they orbit the Earth, waiting to see if they can bring back the breakthrough medicines of the future.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著這些公司持續測試其技術，「太空製造」的夢想正日益接近現實。雖然這仍是一個新興領域，但對患者而言，潛在的益處相當顯著。如果研究人員能成功在軌道的無重力環境中創造出更穩定、更有效的藥物，這將可能改變我們治療許多嚴重疾病的方式。目前，全世界都在注視著這些環繞地球的小型太空艙，等待著看它們是否能帶回未來的突破性藥物。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To sink to the bottom of a liquid.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見意思為「解決（問題）」或「定居」，這裡指物質沉澱。文中：On Earth, gravity causes particles in liquids to settle at the bottom, and it creates currents that move liquids around.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To assume control or responsibility for something previously done by someone or something else.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞 take 和介系詞 over 組成，意思與字面拆開不同。文中：Because of this, several companies are now working to build their own commercial space stations and specialized laboratories to take over the work.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To operate or manage a machine, system, or business.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見意思為「跑步」，這裡指操作或管理工廠設備。文中：For large-scale production, companies need to find ways to run these factories without humans present.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason why Varda Space Industries launched three capsules into orbit?

options.A: To test if humans can survive in space for long periods.
options.B: To produce high-quality crystals for potential cancer treatments.
options.C: To replace the aging International Space Station with new technology.
options.D: To conduct experiments on how semiconductors behave in microgravity.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第一段明確指出，這些膠囊內正在培育能成為抗癌藥物的微小晶體，這是太空製造藥物計畫的一部分。選項 A 文中未提及；選項 C 雖然提到 ISS 即將退休，但 Varda 的目標是製造藥物而非取代該站；選項 D 雖然提到半導體，但那是其他潛在應用，並非 Varda 目前這三顆膠囊的主要任務。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might pharmaceutical companies prefer automated space factories over the current International Space Station (ISS)?

options.A: The ISS is too small to hold the necessary equipment for crystal growth.
options.B: The ISS is too expensive to maintain compared to private capsules.
options.C: Human presence on the ISS poses a risk of contamination to the sensitive manufacturing process.
options.D: The ISS does not have the microgravity conditions required for high-quality production.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。第七段提到，專家指出大規模生產需要無人參與，因為人類會引入灰塵或其他污染物，進而破壞脆弱的晶體生長過程。選項 A 與原文不符，原文強調 ISS 是為科學實驗設計而非大規模生產；選項 B 文中未比較成本；選項 D 錯誤，因為 ISS 確實具備微重力環境，只是不適合大規模自動化生產。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'stable' mean in the context of drug development?

options.A: Resistant to change or degradation over time.
options.C: Able to be produced in large quantities.
options.D: Strong enough to be injected into a vein.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在藥物研發語境中，stable（穩定）指的是藥物在儲存或使用過程中不易變質、分解或失去效力。選項 B 是指物理位置的平衡，不符藥物語境；選項 C 描述的是產能；選項 D 則描述藥物的強度或物理狀態，與「穩定性」定義不符。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: The International Space Station is no longer useful for modern scientific research.
options.B: Space manufacturing is a dangerous but necessary way to develop new electronics.
options.C: Varda Space Industries is the only company capable of producing medicine in space.
options.D: Manufacturing in microgravity offers a promising future for creating better medicines and materials.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心在於探討「太空製造」的潛力，特別是透過微重力環境改善藥物結晶品質與材料性能，儘管目前仍有技術挑戰，但這代表了未來醫療與工業發展的新契機。選項 A 過於誇大；選項 B 忽略了藥物製造才是重點；選項 C 錯誤，因為文中也提到了其他公司如 BioOrbit。
